transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Product), Evan Trimble (CodaMed Head of Platform), Maya Chen (MLE), Liam O'Neill (Director Infra)

Summary:
A focused Optimize console walkthrough to align on INT8 vs FP8 qprofiles, mixed-precision fallback rules, latency SLOs (p95/p99 targets), and next steps to stand up a sandbox pilot. Customer emphasized tight p99 latency requirements for triage path and desire for deterministic fallbacks when quality regressions appear. Security and VPC onboarding briefly discussed.

Topics Covered:
- Quick recap of Redwood Optimize and profile concepts
- Console demo: creating a qprofile, running sandbox evals, visualizing fidelity/latency heatmaps
- INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs and mixed-precision plan for production
- Fallback & canary strategies, rollback paths, telemetry to detect fidelity drift
- Integration notes: batching, KV cache, prefix caching, and SSO/VPC considerations

Action items (captured above) and open questions listed at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, we'll do a short Optimize console walkthrough then dig into the int8 vs fp8 comparisons you've asked for.
[00:18] Evan: sounds good, we have about an hour. main thing is p99 for triage must stay under 280ms, and we need a fallback plan if accuracy dips.
[00:30] Priya: noted, we'll show how qprofile sampling surfaces latency distribution and fidelity delta for your prompt set. also, forgive me if audio sounds rough, connection is a bit patchy today.
[00:46] Maya: no problem, thanks. also want to call out token cost constraints — we budget per token and we run high volume overnight processing.
[00:58] Samir: good, we'll walk throughput/batch tradeoffs too. for overnight batching you might favor larger batch sizes with int8 to reduce cost.
[01:12] Liam: quick infra note, we need VPC peering for private deployment; also we run a FIPS-enabled KMS for key management. where does Redwood land on that?
[01:25] Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer KMS and FIPS HSM integrations; we'll attach the SOC2 + compliance pack in the follow up.
[01:35] Evan: perfect. okay demo time. Priya, take it away on the console.

[02:00] Priya: opening Optimize console — here's the qprofile editor, we start with a baseline (fp16) and then generate candidate profiles: int8 optimized, fp8 standard, and a mixed-precision fallback. you can see we annotate each profile with expected latency, tokens/sec, and a predicted accuracy score (estimated from sampling).
[02:30] Priya: note the UI shows a heatmap of quality vs latency. darker red means bigger fidelity drop; green is acceptable. this is using our internal eval harness but it can run on your seed prompts.
[03:00] Maya: I see a big difference in p99 between int8 and fp8 for long context. is that due to extra dequant overhead?
[03:12] Priya: yeah, for some kernels int8 needs extra reorder/unpack steps — for short sequences int8 often wins on throughput, but for long sequences fp8 holds latency advantage because kernel fusion is better for FP8 in our runtime on A100/NX hardware. sometimes the transcription shows "A one hundred" as "a hundred" — disregard that, small captioning glitch.
[03:40] Jordan: to be clear, our recommendation is run fp8 for latency-sensitive, long-context routes, and int8 for high-throughput short-turn routes. mixed-precision auto-routing can be based on prompt length or route tags.
[04:02] Liam: how deterministic is mixed-precision routing? we need reproducible outputs for audit trails.
[04:12] Priya: routing is deterministic given the rule set — it's config stored in the deployment manifest; rollouts are versioned. we also store a deterministic seed for sampling-based ops. but note that small precision changes can slightly change tokenization boundaries in edge samples.
[04:34] Evan: interesting. show us the fallback behavior when fidelity drops after a model update.
[04:40] Priya: switching to the canary page — you can set a fidelity threshold based on a prompt set. if the sampled fidelity delta exceeds threshold we automatically route to the previous stable profile or escalate to a manual canary hold. demo: I'll push a synthetic delta to the sandbox — you can see the telemetry spike and automatic rollback trigger.
[05:15] (clicks, demo noise)
[05:30] Maya: playback is a bit choppy on our side, but I see the rollback. how are metrics reported? we need p95/p99 and per-route confusion matrices.
[05:45] Priya: metrics include latency distributions, token cost, and fidelity per prompt. confusion matrices for classification tasks are exportable; for generative prompts we provide BLEU/ROUGE style proxies and human-in-the-loop flags.
[06:10] Evan: what's the expected cost delta between int8 and fp8? we care about unit economics.
[06:20] Samir: ballpark — int8 can reduce per-token GPU cost by ~20-35% depending on workload; fp8 sits in between int8 and fp16. but cost depends on throughput efficiency; for small batch low-latency calls fp8 sometimes edges out int8 because of fewer kernel overheads.
[06:45] Liam: so we'd probably run fp8 for our interactive triage UI and int8 for the batch scoring pipeline. any tips to tune batch size without hitting tail latency?
[06:58] Priya: yes — use adaptive batching: small latency-sensitive routes have a cap on batch window (e.g., 10ms) and high-throughput routes have longer windows. Redwood runtime supports continuous batching with priority preemption.
[07:15] Evan: can we get a sample config for that? like a suggested batch_size, max_window_ms per route?
[07:22] Jordan: we'll include a recommended config in the follow up — Priya has a standard template for triage and batch scoring.
[07:30] Maya: one more, how do we measure degradation over time? drift detection?
[07:40] Priya: we have quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; you can schedule periodic sampling and send to our eval runner; any drift beyond set thresholds triggers alerts and stores snapshots for debugging. also we record token-level diffs for quick rollback.
[08:00] Evan: security again — is telemetry PII filtered before leaving our environment for hosted runs?
[08:10] Samir: yes, for hosted we offer redaction; for Private deployments telemetry stays in your VPC and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. we'll note that in the compliance pack.
[08:25] Liam: good. back to quantization specifics — what failure modes have you seen with int8?
[08:33] Priya: some model families exhibit more sensitivity in rare token predictions — hallucination modes slightly increase; we recommend prompt-level holdouts for safety-critical flows and a small human review sample until your qprofile is stable.
[08:50] Maya: can we run an A/B of int8 vs fp8 on a small subset of traffic? we want real user impact not just synthetic evals.
[08:58] Priya: absolutely — console supports traffic splits by route, percent, and canary window. you can route 5% to int8 for 48 hours and compare fidelity and latency slices in the dashboard.
[09:15] Jordan: practical note on rollouts: keep canary at low traffic and set a rollback threshold at, say, 2% absolute fidelity regression or a 10% increase in p99 latency.
[09:30] Evan: good heuristic. can you show the CSV export of the sandbox run? we'd like raw numbers.
[09:38] Priya: exporting now — you'll get per-prompt p95/p99, avg latency, tokens, and fidelity scores. there's also an option to include model trace ids.
[09:50] (file transfer beep)
[10:05] Maya: got it. I noticed the console shows 'prefetch cache' — is that the KV cache? sometimes transcripts show KV as "K V cash" which is weird.
[10:15] Priya: ha — yes KV cache. prefix caching keeps the big KV state to avoid re-computation across similar prompts; it helps a lot for multi-turn. we also offer autosave of hot prefixes.
[10:30] Liam: if we run private on-prem, can we keep prefix cache on local NVMe and still use Redwood control plane?
[10:40] Jordan: yes, in Private we support local cache and customer-managed storage; control plane can be customer-hosted for air-gapped cases. we'll detail ops patterns in the follow up doc.
[11:00] Evan: timeline question — we ideally want a pilot in two weeks with 1) sandbox perf, 2) security review, 3) initial canary on production. feasible?
[11:10] Jordan: doable — sandbox perf and qprofile baselines in one week, security review concurrently (we'll send SOC2+SAML docs), and a tight canary after approvals.
[11:22] Maya: what's the expected data retention for telemetry? we need 90 days minimum.
[11:30] Samir: default is 30 days but enterprise retention add-on supports 90/365; we'll include pricing.
[11:40] Evan: any red flags we should be aware of before we start?
[11:45] Priya: main things: ensure prompt set representative, watch long-tail prompts during int8 tests, and set conservative rollback thresholds initially. also make sure your SRE is ready for VPC peering windows.
[12:00] Jordan: quick recap and next steps — Jordan to share sandbox invite, quickstart, and compliance pack by Friday (2026-04-23). Priya will run int8/fp8 baselines on the sample prompts and share CSVs by Monday (2026-04-27). Evan will confirm SOC2 reviewer and share prompt set by Saturday (2026-04-24).
[12:20] Evan: thanks everyone. looking forward to the sandbox.
[12:30] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up with the links.

Open Questions:
